analysis.title: Americas Construction: Building Products - Non-Residential Construction: Moderation in Data Centers and Multi-Family Drive Non-Res Indicators for October
key_insights: The Dodge Momentum Index fell 9.0% sequentially in October to 260.4 (September revised down to 286.0, vs +2% in September) and is down 2.4% YoY. The decline was led by a slowdown in data center and warehouse planning, while institutional planning was fairly resilient.
The Architecture Billings Index was 44.9 in October vs 44.7 in September, still in contraction. Inquiries have grown for five consecutive months, but the value of newly signed contracts remains weak.

Commercial/industrial billings grew for the third consecutive month (51.0 vs 50.9) and billings at commercial/industrial-focused firms grew for the first time since 2022. Institutional billings fell to 42.5 from 47.6 and multi-family billings slowed this fall.

GS expects a broader, more durable recovery in non-residential activity, particularly new construction, to require a sustained improvement in the economic backdrop. Activity across most sectors is expected to stay under pressure for the next several quarters.

Until the backdrop improves, GS expects healthcare, transportation and education to outperform, supported by industry-specific dynamics. These sectors account for ~60% of AWI's sales, and with greater R&R exposure and company-specific growth initiatives GS maintains its positive view on AWI.
GS is also constructive on CSL, citing the re-roofing cycle, continued innovation, cost improvements, and the shift toward more energy-efficient buildings.

Non-residential exposure in GS coverage: AWI ~95% of revenue and CSL ~80%, so they should benefit most. Owens Corning, A.O. Smith and Mohawk each generate 20+% of sales from non-residential construction.
The ABI declined regionally led by the Midwest (43.0 vs 50.6). The Northeast rose to 40.1 from 39.1, the South to 44.3 from 43.1, and the West held near equilibrium at 49.8 vs 50.7.

Within the Dodge Momentum Index, commercial fell 13.4% sequentially (data centers, warehouses, parking garages, office and hotels, partly offset by retail). Institutional was down 1.5% sequentially but up 33.4% YoY, with healthcare, government and recreational accelerating.
23 projects valued at $100+mn entered planning in October, including three data centers at $365+mn each, two medical projects at $250+mn each and one lab at $200mn.

ABC average non-residential backlog was 8.1 months in October, down 7% sequentially and 4% YoY. Commercial & industrial fell 11% to 9.0 months and infrastructure fell 7% to 9.4 months, while heavy industrial rose 24% YoY to 10.1 months. Infrastructure backlog hit its lowest level since May 2025 and heavy industrial a 15-month high.

The ABC Construction Confidence Index for sales was flat at 59.9. 48% of respondents expect a slight sales increase over the next 6 months (47% prior), 9% a significant increase (8% prior), and 21% a decline (20% prior).

Office utilization across the top 10 metros was 56.5% as of October 28 per Kastle, up 110bps sequentially and 170bps YoY, and 40bps below the post-pandemic high of 56.9% in March. Five of 10 metros rose (Austin +9%, New York +6%, San Francisco +1%) and San Jose fell 2%.
Total office employment in September was flat sequentially and YoY at 34.4mn jobs, 4% above October 2019, which GS says supports future office construction and R&R activity.

tension_points.bull_case: Commercial/industrial billings grew for the first time since 2022 at firms focused on that segment, and inquiries have risen for five consecutive months. Institutional planning is resilient (+33.4% YOY), and 56% of ABC members expect sales to increase.
tension_points.bear_case: The ABI remains below 50 at 44.9 and the value of signed contracts is weak. The Dodge Momentum Index fell 9.0% sequentially, and ABC backlog fell 7% sequentially and 4% YOY. A durable recovery in new construction needs a better economic backdrop.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained improvement in the economic backdrop would be needed for a broader, more durable recovery in non-residential activity.
